mainTopic: The four yearly judgments, who authored the משנה, daily judgment and prayer, and the reasons for the seasonal מצוות and שופר
overview: The משנה lists four times each year when the world is judged: פסח for grain, שבועות for tree fruit, ראש השנה for every person, and סוכות for rain. The גמרא shows that grain is judged twice, and אביי draws a farming tip from this. It then asks who wrote the משנה, since it fits none of the views of רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי, or רבי נתן in a ברייתא. רבא answers that it follows the school of רבי ישמעאל, and that the משנה speaks only of when people's judgment begins. רב חסדא finds a better verse for רבי יוסי's view that a person is judged daily. He also teaches from that verse that a king is judged before the community. רב יוסף explains that our daily prayers for the sick fit either רבי יוסי or רבנן, because crying out helps even after the גזר דין. A ברייתא then explains that the עומר, שתי הלחם, water pouring, and the ראש השנה prayers each ask for blessing on what is judged at that season, and רבי אבהו explains why the שופר is a ram's horn. Finally, רבי יצחק's question is narrowed down to why we blow while sitting before the עמידה, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Four times a year the world is judged
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists four judgment times: grain on פסח, tree fruit on שבועות, all people on ראש השנה, and water on סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are four times a year when the world is judged. On פסח, the judgment is about grain. On שבועות, it is about fruit that grows on trees. On ראש השנה, every person passes before ה׳ one by one, like sheep, as the פסוק says: 'He Who forms all their hearts together, Who understands all their deeds.' On סוכות, the world is judged about water (rain).
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a list of four yearly judgment days and says what is judged on each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each festival matches the subject judged at that time of year. Grain is near harvest at פסח, tree fruit is ripening at שבועות, and the rainy season begins after סוכות. ראש השנה is different because it judges every person, not a crop. The פסוק proves that ה׳ looks at each person individually.

keyTerms.meaning: Set times or seasons of the year
Like sheep passing one at a time, meaning each person is judged individually

steps.whatToRemember: פסח = grain, שבועות = tree fruit, ראש השנה = people, סוכות = water.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
At four times of the year the world is judged:
On Pesach, concerning the grain;
On Shavuot, concerning the fruits of the tree;
On Rosh Hashanah, all who come into the world
pass before Him like sheep, one by one,
as it is said: 'He Who fashions their hearts together,'
'Who understands all their deeds' (Tehillim 33:15);
and on the Festival (Sukkot) they are judged concerning the water.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The world is judged four times a year, each time on a different subject: grain, tree fruit, people, and water.

steps.title: Which grain is judged on פסח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which grain the משנה means when it says grain is judged on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which grain is being judged on פסח?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a short clarifying question about the first case in the משנה. This sets up the next step, where it tests a possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At פסח there are two kinds of grain to think about: grain already standing in the field and grain that will be planted later. The משנה does not say which one it means, so the גמרא asks.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Which grain?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of 'grain' in the משנה's פסח case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the grain judged on פסח is the grain now standing in the field or the grain that will be sown in the coming year.

steps.title: It cannot mean grain already standing in the field
steps.stepSummary: If פסח judged the standing grain, then everything that already happened to that grain over the winter would never have been judged.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means the grain already standing in the field, then all the things that happened to it while it grew over the winter, when were those judged?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possible answer and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The standing grain has already been through a whole winter of weather and events. If its judgment came only now at פסח, all those earlier events would have happened with no judgment behind them. That cannot be right, so the standing grain cannot be what the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a possibility the גמרא is about to reject)
That is standing (already growing in the field)
Events, things that happen to something

phrases.english: If you say it is this grain that is already standing,
then all these events that already passed over it,
when were they judged?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to the question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading 'grain' in the משנה as the grain currently standing in the field.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Under that reading, the events that happened to the grain during the winter, before פסח, would never have been judged.

steps.title: It means grain that is about to be sown
steps.stepSummary: The judgment on פסח is about the grain that will be planted in the coming year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means grain that is going to be sown.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the first possibility, the גמרא gives its answer: the פסח judgment is about future crops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A judgment decided ahead of time covers everything that will happen to the crop from planting onward. This avoids the problem of earlier events going unjudged.

keyTerms.meaning: That is going to be sown

phrases.english: Rather, it is the grain that is going to be sown.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct answer after the first option was rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסח judgment is about the grain that will be sown in the coming year.

steps.title: Challenge from a ברייתא: is there only one judgment?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a crop gets only one judgment, and quotes a ברייתא showing that one crop can fall under two different פסח judgments.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean only one judgment is made for a crop? But a ברייתא teaches: If grain has a mishap or accident before פסח, it was judged in the past, at last פסח. If it happens after פסח, it was judged this פסח for the future. Similarly, if a person has a mishap or accident before יום הכיפורים, he was judged in the past, last year. If it happens after יום הכיפורים, he was judged this year for the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that a crop is judged only once, using a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture one crop that is planted in the winter and harvested after פסח. The ברייתא says a mishap before פסח comes from last פסח's judgment, and a mishap after פסח comes from this פסח's judgment. So the same crop is covered by two judgments, which seems to contradict the idea that each crop is judged only once, when it is about to be sown.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say...? (introduces a challenge to an implication)
An accident caused by outside force
For the past, under the earlier judgment
For the future, under the new judgment

steps.confusionAlert: Here קרי does NOT mean the halachic term for ritual impurity from an emission. It comes from 'מקרה' and simply means a chance mishap.

phrases.english: Is this to say that only one judgment is made?
But isn't it taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: תְּבוּאָה שֶׁאֵירַע בָּהּ קֶרִי אוֹ אוֹנֶס,
phrases.english: Grain that suffered a mishap or an accident:
if before Pesach, it was judged in the past (last Pesach);
if after Pesach, it was judged for the future (this Pesach).

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם שֶׁאֵירַע בּוֹ קֶרִי אוֹ אוֹנֶס,
phrases.english: A person who suffered a mishap or an accident:
if before Yom Kippur, he was judged in the past (last year);
if after Yom Kippur, he was judged for the future (this year).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what step 4 implies, namely that a crop is judged only once, before it is sown.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that each crop receives a single judgment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא splits one crop's mishaps between last פסח's judgment and this פסח's judgment, so a single crop falls under two judgments.

steps.title: רבא: grain is judged twice
steps.stepSummary: רבא accepts the ברייתא and concludes that a crop is judged twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Learn from this that two judgments are made.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא resolves the challenge by accepting it: a crop really does receive two judgments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain planted before פסח is judged at the previous פסח for its early growth. It is judged again at this פסח for the rest of its growth until harvest. This fits both the ברייתא and the answer that the judgment is about grain that is going to be sown.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it (a conclusion drawn from a source)

steps.whatToRemember: A crop that grows across פסח is judged twice: last פסח covers the period before פסח, and this פסח covers the period after it.

phrases.english: Rava said: Learn from here
that two judgments are made.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ תְּרֵי דִינֵי מִתַּדְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge by drawing a new conclusion from the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the challenge and refines the rule: there are two judgments instead of one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought each crop is judged only once, at the פסח before it is sown.
steps.terutzMaskana: A crop growing across פסח is judged twice, once for each stage of its growth.

steps.title: אביי's farming advice based on two judgments
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that if a farmer sees his late crops doing well, he should quickly plant early crops, which will ripen before the next judgment.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Therefore, if a person sees that his late-ripening crops are doing well, he should hurry and plant early-ripening crops. Before they reach the next judgment, they will already have grown.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws a practical lesson from רבא's conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the slow crops are succeeding, this year's judgment was clearly good. A fast crop like barley, planted now, will ripen before the next פסח judgment, so it is fully covered by this good judgment. This applies רבא's rule that each judgment covers its own period.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the idea of two judgments is not only theoretical. It affects how a person can sensibly plan around a good year.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Therefore,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי חָזֵי אִינָשׁ דְּמַצְלַח זַרְעָא אַפְלָא —
phrases.english: when a person sees that the late-ripening crop is succeeding,
he should hurry and sow an early-ripening crop,
for by the time it reaches its judgment,
it will already have grown.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבא's two-judgment conclusion to a practical case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because each judgment covers its own period, a farmer who sees a good year should plant fast crops that will ripen before the next judgment.

steps.title: No known opinion matches the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the author of the משנה is, and claims it fits none of four תנאים: רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי, or רבי נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is our משנה? It is not רבי מאיר, not רבי יהודה, not רבי יוסי, and not רבי נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about four judgment times and asks who could have said it. It announces that none of the four known opinions fits, and the next step brings the ברייתא to show why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is more than a request for information. It is a problem: the משנה seems to stand alone, without any known תנא behind it. The proof comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? Asks who the author of a text is

phrases.english: Whose is our Mishnah?

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Not Rabbi Meir, and not Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, וְלָא רַבִּי נָתָן.
phrases.english: and not Rabbi Yosei, and not Rabbi Natan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic. It turns from the farming discussion to the question of who wrote the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The authorship of the משנה about four judgment times
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every known opinion on when judgment happens differs from the משנה, so the משנה seems to have no author.

steps.title: The opinions of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says: רבי מאיר holds that everything is judged on ראש השנה and sealed on יום הכיפורים. רבי יהודה holds that everything is judged on ראש השנה, but each item is sealed at its own time: grain on פסח, fruit on עצרת, water on סוכות, and people on יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the ברייתא teaches: Everything is judged on ראש השנה, and the verdict is sealed on יום הכיפורים. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: Everything is judged on ראש השנה, and each verdict is sealed at its own time. On פסח, for grain. On עצרת, for tree fruit. On סוכות they are judged for water. And a person is judged on ראש השנה, and his verdict is sealed on יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא to prove its claim, starting with the first two opinions. Neither רבי מאיר nor רבי יהודה says what the משנה says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר has only one judgment day for everything, but the משנה has four. רבי יהודה has four times, but he calls them times of 'sealing.' He places the actual judging of everything on ראש השנה. The משנה, however, says the world is 'judged' on פסח, עצרת, and סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'judged' (נידון) with 'sealed' (נחתם). For רבי יהודה, the judging of everything happens on ראש השנה. Only the sealing is spread out over the year.

phrases.english: As it is taught: All are judged on Rosh HaShana,

phrases.aramaic: וּגְזַר דִּין שֶׁלָּהֶם נֶחְתָּם בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים,
phrases.english: and their verdict is sealed on Yom Kippur;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: הַכֹּל נִידּוֹנִין בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: All are judged on Rosh HaShana,
and their verdict is sealed
each one at its own time:
on Passover, regarding grain;
on Shavuot, regarding tree fruit;
on Sukkot they are judged regarding water.
And a person is judged on Rosh HaShana,

phrases.aramaic: וּגְזַר דִּין שֶׁלּוֹ נֶחְתָּם בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.
phrases.english: and his verdict is sealed on Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that proves the claim in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה does not follow רבי מאיר or רבי יהודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא recording the views of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה

steps.title: The opinions of רבי יוסי and רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says a person is judged every day. רבי נתן says a person is judged every hour. Each brings a verse from איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: A person is judged every day, as it says: 'You visit him every morning.' רבי נתן says: A person is judged every hour, as it says: 'You test him every moment.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with two more opinions. Both are clearly different from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says people are judged once a year, on ראש השנה. רבי יוסי says people are judged daily, and רבי נתן says hourly. So neither of them can be the author of the משנה, and this completes the proof that no listed opinion fits.

keyTerms.meaning: You visit (examine) him every morning (איוב ז:יח)
You test him every moment (איוב ז:יח)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אָדָם נִידּוֹן בְּכׇל יוֹם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: A person is judged every day,
as it is stated: "You visit him every morning."

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: אָדָם נִידּוֹן בְּכׇל שָׁעָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says: A person is judged every hour,
as it is stated: "You test him every moment."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אָדָם נִידּוֹן בְּכׇל יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and finishes the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה does not follow רבי יוסי or רבי נתן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא, together with verses from איוב

steps.title: Suggestion: the משנה follows רבי יהודה and means sealing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה really is רבי יהודה. When the משנה says 'judged,' it means the verdict is sealed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: Really, the משנה is רבי יהודה. When the משנה teaches its four times, it is speaking about the sealing of the verdict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible way to save the משנה by linking it to רבי יהודה. This sets up a test, and the very next step will check whether it works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's sealing times for grain (פסח), fruit (עצרת), and water (סוכות) match the משנה exactly. So if the משנה's word 'judged' just means 'sealed,' the problem seems solved.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a suggested answer)

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא,
phrases.english: And if you will say: Really, it is Rabbi Yehuda,
and when the Mishnah teaches, it refers to the sealing of the verdict,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the problem from step 8 by reading the משנה's wording differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a word in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'judged' cannot match any תנא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read 'judged' as 'sealed,' and the משנה fits רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The suggestion fails because of people
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion does not work. For people, רבי יהודה says the sealing is on יום הכיפורים, but the משנה says ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, there is a difficulty from the case of a person!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 11. Reading 'judged' as 'sealed' breaks down for the משנה's line about people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists ראש השנה as the time for all people. According to רבי יהודה, a person's verdict is sealed on יום הכיפורים, not ראש השנה. So the 'sealing' reading cannot fit the whole משנה, and in the next step רבא names a different author.
steps.whatToRemember: No תנא in the ברייתא fits the משנה. Even רבי יהודה fails, because for people his sealing day is יום הכיפורים, while the משנה names ראש השנה.

phrases.english: If so, the case of a person is difficult!
phrases.notes: For רבי יהודה, a person's sealing is on יום הכיפורים, but the משנה says ראש השנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested answer of step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole suggestion that the משנה means 'sealing' according to רבי יהודה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: For people, רבי יהודה's sealing day is יום הכיפורים, but the משנה lists ראש השנה.

steps.title: רבא: The משנה follows the school of רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the question of who wrote the משנה. It is a תנא from the school of רבי ישמעאל, who taught that the world is judged at four times: grain on פסח, fruit on עצרת, water on סוכות, and people on ראש השנה, with their verdict sealed on יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is the תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל. The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: The world is judged at four times. On פסח it is judged on grain. On עצרת it is judged on tree fruit. On סוכות it is judged on water. A person is judged on ראש השנה, and his verdict is sealed on יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finally answers its question about who wrote the משנה. רבא names a fifth source, the school of רבי ישמעאל, whose teaching fits the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four תנאים in steps 8–12 did not fit the משנה. This ברייתא matches it: the three crops are judged at their own festivals, and people are judged on ראש השנה. It adds one detail the משנה left out, that the verdict on people is sealed on יום הכיפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: The study hall (school) of רבי ישמעאל
Set times or seasons of the year

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הִיא,
phrases.english: This is the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael,
phrases.notes: The answer to who the author of the משנה is.

phrases.english: as the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
At four times the world is judged:
On Pesach, concerning the grain;
on Atzeret (Shavuot), concerning the fruits of the tree;
on the Festival (Sukkot), they are judged concerning the water.
And a person is judged on Rosh HaShanah,

phrases.aramaic: וּגְזַר דִּין שֶׁלּוֹ נֶחְתָּם בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.
phrases.english: and his verdict is sealed on Yom Kippur.
phrases.notes: This adds a detail that the משנה does not mention.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַאי תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the attempt to match the משנה to רבי יהודה failed in step 12, רבא offers a new author whose view fits.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a different תנא as the author
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No known תנא matches the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows the school of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the school of רבי ישמעאל

steps.title: The משנה speaks about the start of judgment
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the verdict on people is sealed on יום הכיפורים. The משנה mentions only ראש השנה because it is describing when the judgment begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when our משנה teaches that people are judged on ראש השנה, it means the beginning of the judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the משנה fits the ברייתא even though the משנה never mentions יום הכיפורים. The משנה is only talking about when the judgment starts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the reverse of the failed attempt in step 11. There the word 'judged' was read as 'sealed,' which did not work for people. Here 'judged' means the opening of the case on ראש השנה, while the sealing on יום הכיפורים is simply left unsaid.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה follows the school of רבי ישמעאל. People are judged on ראש השנה, which is the start, and the verdict is sealed on יום הכיפורים.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 11. There, 'judged' was read as 'sealed.' Here, 'judged' means 'the judgment begins.'

phrases.english: And when the Mishnah teaches it, it refers to the beginning of the judgment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adjusts the reading of the משנה so it fully matches the ברייתא in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה says people are judged only on ראש השנה, with nothing after it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is describing only the start of the judgment.

steps.title: רב חסדא asks for רבי יוסי's reason
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks what the source is for רבי יוסי's view that a person is judged every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: What is the reason for רבי יוסי's view?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב חסדא asks why רבי יוסי holds that a person is judged every day, and this sets up the next few steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's view was quoted in step 10. רב חסדא is not asking about the משנה anymore. He wants to understand the reasoning behind רבי יוסי's opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, a sage of the גמרא period

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the question of who wrote the משנה and returns to רבי יוסי's view from step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי יוסי's view that a person is judged daily

steps.title: But רבי יוסי already gave his verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised by רב חסדא's question, because רבי יוסי already quoted his source: ״ותפקדנו לבקרים״.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why ask? He already gave his reason: ״You visit him every morning.״
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's question. רבי יוסי already gave a verse, so it seems there is nothing to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא of step 10, רבי יוסי supported his view with the verse ״ותפקדנו לבקרים״ from איוב. It seems pointless to ask for a reason that was already stated.

keyTerms.meaning: As he himself stated his reason

phrases.english: As he stated his reason:
"And You visit him every morning"!
phrases.notes: איוב ז:יח. רבי יוסי's verse from the ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the question in step 15 needed to be asked at all.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי already stated a verse, so the question has an obvious answer.

steps.title: The real question: why not follow רבי נתן?
steps.stepSummary: The question was really this: why didn't רבי יוסי agree with רבי נתן that a person is judged every hour? One might answer that רבי נתן's verse uses the word בחינה, which means only an examination and not real judgment.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what we meant: why didn't he hold like רבי נתן? If you say that בחינה, 'trying,' is just an examination…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רב חסדא was really asking. Then it suggests a possible reason why רבי יוסי did not accept רבי נתן's verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן's verse is ״לרגעים תבחננו״, 'You try him every moment.' It would prove judgment every hour. רבי יוסי might reject it because בחינה could mean only looking someone over, not an actual verdict.

keyTerms.meaning: Trying, testing (the word in רבי נתן's verse)
Just looking over, a mere examination

phrases.english: This is what we are saying:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי נָתָן?
phrases.english: What is the reason he did not say like Rabbi Natan?
If you say that 'trying' is merely examination,
phrases.notes: This is a suggested reason for rejecting רבי נתן's verse, "לרגעים תבחננו".

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנַן הָכִי קָאָמְרִינַן: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 by restating רב חסדא's question in a sharper way.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא was asking for a source that was already known.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was asking why רבי יוסי rejected רבי נתן's verse. The possible reason is that בחינה means only an examination.

steps.title: Visiting is also just examination
steps.stepSummary: The suggested reason fails. If בחינה is only an examination, then פקידה, the word in רבי יוסי's own verse, is also only an examination.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then פקידה, 'visiting,' is also just an examination!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the reason given in step 17. רבי יוסי's own verse would have the same weakness he found in רבי נתן's verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whatever argument removes רבי נתן's verse also removes רבי יוסי's verse. So ״ותפקדנו לבקרים״ cannot prove daily judgment. This forces a search for a new source.

keyTerms.meaning: Visiting, checking on (the word in רבי יוסי's verse)

phrases.english: Then 'visiting' is also merely examination!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the distinction suggested in step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It removes ״ותפקדנו לבקרים״ as a proof for רבי יוסי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: פקידה has the same weakness as בחינה, since both may mean only an examination.

steps.title: רב חסדא brings a new verse for רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא brings a different source for רבי יוסי from מלכים: ״to make the judgment of His servant and the judgment of His people Israel, each day as it requires.״
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב חסדא said: רבי יוסי's reason comes from here: ״To make the judgment of His servant and the judgment of His people Israel, the matter of each day on its day.״
steps.whatsHappening: The first verse did not work, so רב חסדא gives a new verse that clearly talks about judgment every day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This verse uses the word משפט, 'judgment,' so the problem of 'mere examination' does not apply. The words ״דבר יום ביומו״ show that this judgment happens every day.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejecting what came before and offering something new)
Each day's matter on its own day, meaning daily

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי's view that a person is judged daily comes from ״לעשות משפט... דבר יום ביומו״, not from ״ותפקדנו לבקרים״.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Chisda said:
Rabbi Yosei's reason is from here:
"To make the judgment of His servant
and the judgment of His people Israel,
the matter of each day on its day."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the verse that was rejected in step 18 with a better source.
steps.terutzMaskana: His source is ״לעשות משפט... דבר יום ביומו״, which clearly speaks of judgment.

steps.title: A king is judged before the community
steps.stepSummary: Using the same verse, רב חסדא teaches that when a king and a community are judged, the king's case comes first, because the verse says 'His servant' before 'His people Israel.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: When a king and a community are judged, the king comes into judgment first, as it says: ״To make the judgment of His servant and the judgment of His people Israel.״
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא learns a second lesson from the same verse. The king, called 'His servant,' is judged before the people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of the words in the verse is the proof. 'His servant' refers to the king, who is mentioned first, and 'His people Israel' comes after.

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:
A king and a community:
the king enters into judgment first,
as it is stated: "To make the judgment of His servant
and the judgment of His people Israel."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the verse from step 19 to teach a new, related idea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In heavenly judgment, a king is judged before the community.

steps.title: Why does the king go first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason the king is judged before the community.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the king should be judged first. This sets up two possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse shows that the king goes first. Now the גמרא wants to know the logic behind that order.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the rule in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the king is judged first

steps.title: First reason: a king should not wait outside
steps.stepSummary: First answer: it is not respectful for a king to wait outside while his people are judged.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: it is not proper conduct for a king to sit outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first reason. It is about honoring the king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the people went first, the king would have to wait outside until their case ended. That would not be fitting for his honor.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces one of two possible answers)

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
it is not proper conduct
for the king to sit outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The king's honor: he should not have to wait outside.

steps.title: Second reason: before anger grows
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: the king is judged first, before Divine anger grows because of the community's sins, so that he is judged more gently.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: so that he is judged before the anger grows strong.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different reason. This one is for the king's own benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the people's sins are reviewed, Divine anger may grow stronger. Judging the king first protects him from a harsher verdict.
steps.whatToRemember: A king is judged before the community. The two reasons are his honor, so he does not wait outside, and his protection, so he is judged before anger grows.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
before the burning anger increases.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: מִקַּמֵּי דְּלִיפּוֹשׁ חֲרוֹן אַף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, separate answer to the question in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The king's protection: he is judged before anger over the community's sins grows.

steps.title: Whose opinion do our daily prayers for the sick follow?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks which opinion supports our custom of praying every day for sick and suffering people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: According to whose opinion do we pray nowadays for the sick and the suffering?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף raises a question about our everyday prayer practice. He is setting up the answer that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned a disagreement about when people are judged. If judgment happens only once a year, why pray every day for the sick? רב יוסף wants to know which side of that disagreement our custom matches.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
According to whom do we pray nowadays
for the sick and the afflicted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the earlier dispute about when people are judged to a practical prayer custom.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion about the timing of judgment explains our daily prayer for the sick?

steps.title: Answer: it follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: Our daily prayers fit רבי יוסי, who holds that a person is judged every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom? According to רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers his own question. The custom follows רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי holds that people are judged every day. So every day there is a fresh judgment that prayer can affect. That makes daily prayer for the sick fully logical.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who holds that a person is judged every day

phrases.english: According to whom? According to Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The custom follows רבי יוסי's view of daily judgment.

steps.title: Second answer: it can even follow רבנן
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, the custom can match רבנן, who hold that judgment is once a year, when combined with רבי יצחק's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: really it follows רבנן, together with the teaching of רבי יצחק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to explain the custom. It does not have to follow רבי יוסי at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if judgment happens only once a year, prayer could still help after the decision has been made. If so, daily prayer makes sense according to רבנן as well. The next step quotes רבי יצחק to back this up.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces an alternative answer)
The Sages (here, those who hold judgment is once a year)

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not say רבנן agree with רבי יוסי about daily judgment. They still hold judgment is once a year. The point is only that prayer can help even after the judgment.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
actually it is according to the Rabbis,
and according to Rabbi Yitzchak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of step 24, instead of the answer in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The custom fits רבנן too, because prayer helps even after the decree.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: crying out helps before and after the גזר דין
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that crying out to ה׳ is good for a person both before and after the גזר דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יצחק said: Crying out is good for a person, both before the decree and after the decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יצחק's statement, which is the basis for the second answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If prayer can change things even after the decree, then a once-a-year judgment does not make daily prayer pointless. This is how the custom can fit רבנן.
steps.whatToRemember: Daily prayer for the sick works on either view: according to רבי יוסי, because judgment is daily, and according to רבנן, because prayer helps even after the גזר דין.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Crying out is good for a person
both before the decree
and after the decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the alternative answer in step 26.
steps.raayaObject: That daily prayer for the sick can follow רבנן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יצחק's statement that crying out helps even after the גזר דין.

steps.title: Why the עומר is brought on פסח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from רבי עקיבא: the עומר is brought on פסח, the grain season, so that the grain in the fields will be blessed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה said in the name of רבי עקיבא: Why did the Torah say to bring the עומר on פסח? Because פסח is the time of grain. ה׳ said: Bring the עומר before Me on פסח, so that the grain in the fields will be blessed for you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching. It explains why the עומר offering is brought specifically on פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each offering is matched to the season when that crop's fate is being decided. On פסח the grain is ripening, so we bring a grain offering then to draw blessing onto it. This connects to the earlier idea that the world is judged for grain on פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
The barley offering brought on the second day of פסח
So that it will be blessed

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the pattern for the whole ברייתא: the מצוה of each season is a request for blessing on what is being judged at that time.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda said in the name of Rabbi Akiva:
For what reason did the Torah say
bring the omer on Pesach?
Because Pesach is the time of grain,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Bring the omer before Me on Pesach,
so that the grain in the fields will be blessed for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about the reasons for the seasonal מצוות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עומר is brought on פסח so that the grain will be blessed.

steps.title: Why the שתי הלחם are brought on שבועות
steps.stepSummary: The שתי הלחם are brought on עצרת, the season of tree fruit, so that the tree fruit will be blessed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did the Torah say to bring the שתי הלחם on עצרת? Because עצרת is the time of tree fruit. ה׳ said: Bring the שתי הלחם before Me on עצרת, so that the tree fruit will be blessed for you.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the same pattern, now for שבועות (עצרת).
steps.deeperAnalysis: עצרת is when the world is judged for fruit of the tree. Bringing the שתי הלחם then is a request for blessing on those fruits. Notice that a wheat offering brings blessing on tree fruit, because what matters is the timing.

keyTerms.meaning: The two wheat loaves offered on שבועות

phrases.english: And for what reason did the Torah say
bring the two loaves on Shavuos?

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁעֲצֶרֶת זְמַן פֵּירוֹת הָאִילָן הוּא,
phrases.english: Because Shavuos is the time of tree fruit,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Bring the two loaves before Me on Shavuos,
so that the tree fruit will be blessed for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה הָבִיאוּ שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם בָּעֲצֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second item in the same ברייתא, following the same pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שתי הלחם are brought on עצרת so that the tree fruit will be blessed.

steps.title: Why water is poured on סוכות
steps.stepSummary: Water is poured on the מזבח on סוכות so that the rains of the year will be blessed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did the Torah say to pour water on the festival of סוכות‎? ה׳ said: Pour water before Me on the festival, so that the rains of the year will be blessed for you.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with ניסוך המים on סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סוכות is when the world is judged for rain, and the rainy season begins right after it. Pouring water on the מזבח is a request for good rain. This also hints that ניסוך המים comes from the Torah, as רבי עקיבא holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Pour (as a libation on the מזבח)

phrases.english: And for what reason did the Torah say
pour water on the festival?
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Pour water before Me on the festival,
so that the rains of the year will be blessed for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה נַסְּכוּ מַיִם בֶּחָג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third item in the ברייתא, again following the same pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water is poured on סוכות so that the year's rain will be blessed.

steps.title: מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות on ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: On ראש השנה we say מלכיות to crown ה׳‎, זכרונות so that we are remembered for good, and this is done through the שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And say before Me on ראש השנה מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות. מלכיות, so that you crown Me as King over you. זכרונות, so that your remembrance rises before Me for good. And with what? With the שופר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by explaining the three special sections of the ראש השנה prayers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the day of judgment, we first accept ה׳ as King. Then we ask to be remembered for good. The שופר is the means through which that remembrance goes up. So the שופר is not a separate idea but the tool that carries the other two.

keyTerms.meaning: That you will crown Me as King

phrases.english: And say before Me on Rosh Hashanah
Kingships, Remembrances, and Shofaros.
Kingships, so that you will crown Me King over you;

phrases.aramaic: זִכְרוֹנוֹת — כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה זִכְרוֹנְיכֶם לְפָנַי לְטוֹבָה,
phrases.english: Remembrances, so that your remembrance will rise before Me for good;
and with what? With the shofar.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִמְרוּ לְפָנַי בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה מַלְכִיּוֹת זִכְרוֹנוֹת וְשׁוֹפָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final part of the ברייתא, moving from the festival offerings to the ראש השנה prayers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ראש השנה we say מלכיות and זכרונות, and the remembrance rises through the שופר.
steps.whatToRemember: Each season's מצוה asks for blessing on what is being judged then: the עומר for grain, the שתי הלחם for fruit, the water for rain. On ראש השנה, the day of judgment, we crown ה׳ and ask to be remembered for good through the שופר.

steps.title: Why the שופר is a ram's horn
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that we blow a ram's horn so that ה׳ will remember עקידת יצחק and treat us as if we had bound ourselves before Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: Why do we blow with a ram's horn? ה׳ said: Blow before Me with a ram's horn, so that I will remember for you the binding of יצחק son of אברהם, and I will count it for you as if you had bound yourselves before Me.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו adds a teaching in the same style. He explains why the שופר specifically comes from a ram.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the עקידה a ram was offered in place of יצחק. Blowing a ram's horn reminds ה׳ of that moment. ה׳ then credits us as if we ourselves had shown the same total devotion. This builds on the previous step's idea that our remembrance rises through the שופר.

keyTerms.meaning: I will count it for you

steps.whatToRemember: The ram's-horn שופר brings up the merit of עקידת יצחק, and ה׳ counts it as if we had bound ourselves before Him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
Why do we blow with a ram's-horn shofar?
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Blow before Me with a ram's-horn shofar,
so that I will remember for you
the binding of Isaac son of Abraham,
and I will count it for you
as if you had bound yourselves before Me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: לָמָה תּוֹקְעִין בְּשׁוֹפָר שֶׁל אַיִל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the ברייתא's teaching about the שופר by explaining why it must be a ram's horn.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ram's horn is used so that ה׳ will remember עקידת יצחק in our favor.

steps.title: רבי יצחק asks why we blow on ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק opens with a question: why do we blow the שופר on ראש השנה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: Why do we blow the שופר on ראש השנה?
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching from רבי יצחק begins with a question about why we blow the שופר. The גמרא will soon push back on how the question is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous steps gave reasons for Temple and holiday practices, such as the עומר, שתי הלחם, and water pouring. רבי יצחק continues that theme by asking about the reason behind the שופר blasts. As worded, the question sounds like it is asking why we blow at all.

keyTerms.meaning: We blow (the שופר); also refers to the long, straight blast called תקיעה
The Jewish New Year, the day of שופר blowing

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
phrases.notes: Attribution line, merged into this step.

phrases.english: Why do we blow on Rosh Hashanah?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: לָמָּה תּוֹקְעִין בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of reasons for holiday practices with a new question about שופר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason we blow the שופר on ראש השנה.

steps.title: The Torah already commands us to blow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised: how can you ask why we blow, when the verse says 'תקעו', 'blow'?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Why do we blow?!' The Merciful One (the Torah) said 'Blow!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the question itself. There is no need to ask why we blow, because a פסוק commands it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a פסוק explicitly commands an act, asking 'why do we do it?' makes no sense as a practical question. The answer is simply 'because ה׳ said so.' The verse is 'תקעו בחודש שופר' (תהלים פ״א:ד׳). So רבי יצחק must have meant something else.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One', meaning ה׳ / the Torah
'Blow!', the command in the פסוק 'תקעו בחודש שופר'

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not doubting the מצוה of שופר. It is objecting to the wording of רבי יצחק's question, because a direct Torah command needs no other explanation.

phrases.english: Why do we blow?!
phrases.notes: Said in astonishment, repeating the question.

phrases.english: The Merciful One said, 'Blow!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of רבי יצחק's question.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An explicit פסוק commands blowing, so the question has an obvious answer and cannot be what רבי יצחק meant.

steps.title: Maybe the question is about the תרועה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the question: perhaps רבי יצחק asked why we also blow a תרועה (broken blasts).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he meant: Why do we blow a תרועה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to save the question by reading it differently. Maybe רבי יצחק was asking about the תרועה, the broken blasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the plain תקיעה is clearly commanded, maybe the puzzle is why we add the broken-sounding תרועה. This is a new reading of the same question. The גמרא will test it next.

keyTerms.meaning: We blow a תרועה, the broken or staccato blasts

phrases.english: Rather: why do we blow a teruah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge by reinterpreting רבי יצחק's question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was about blowing at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question was about why we add the תרועה.

steps.title: The Torah also commands the תרועה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects again: the Torah says 'זכרון תרועה', so the תרועה is also commanded.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Why do we blow a תרועה?!' The Merciful One said 'a remembrance of תרועה'!
steps.whatsHappening: The new reading also fails. The Torah explicitly mentions the תרועה, so there is no need to ask why we do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same logic as before applies. The פסוק in ויקרא כ״ג:כ״ד calls the day 'זכרון תרועה', so the תרועה is a direct Torah command. The question must be about something the Torah does not state.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A remembrance of תרועה', the Torah's description of ראש השנה (ויקרא כ״ג:כ״ד)
The broken or staccato שופר blast

phrases.english: We blow a teruah?!
The Merciful One said, 'a remembrance of teruah'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the second reading using the same reasoning as step 34.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading 'why do we blow a תרועה?'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תרועה is explicitly commanded in the Torah, so asking its reason as a practical question is pointless.

steps.title: The real question: blowing while sitting and again while standing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא settles on the true question: why do we blow תקיעה and תרועה while the people are sitting (before the עמידה), and then again while standing?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he meant: Why do we blow תקיעה and תרועה while the people are sitting, [and again while they are standing]?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finally finds a question that makes sense: why do we have a set of blasts while sitting, before the עמידה, in addition to the blasts during the עמידה? This sets up רבי יצחק's answer, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah commands blowing, but it does not say to blow twice, once sitting and once standing. That extra set, the תקיעות דמיושב, is a practice that needs a reason. The sentence continues on the next amud, so the explanation is still to come.

keyTerms.meaning: While they (the congregation) are sitting, before the עמידה
The 'sitting blasts' blown before מוסף, not during the עמידה

steps.confusionAlert: 'Sitting' here does not mean the person blowing must sit. It refers to the first set of blasts, blown before the congregation stands for the עמידה.
steps.whatToRemember: Through two rejections, the גמרא narrows רבי יצחק's question. Not 'why blow?' and not 'why blow a תרועה?' (both are Torah commands), but 'why blow an extra set while sitting before the עמידה?'

phrases.english: Rather: why do we blow tekiah and teruah
while they are sitting,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud ('and again while standing').

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: לָמָּה תּוֹקְעִין וּמְרִיעִין כְּשֶׁהֵן יוֹשְׁבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final, correct reading of רבי יצחק's question after both earlier readings were rejected.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why we blow an extra set of תקיעות and תרועות while sitting before the עמידה, beyond the blasts commanded by the Torah.
